messages.author: 97698fee6c0bd52a
messages.subject: Exported Files with NA identifier
parts:
Hi All, 

Christopher and I are working on activity classification from the exported files meta/ms5.outraw/. 

When executing the function g.shell.GGIR() for two input files with names,
- 001113_28873.cwa
- 002492_41265.cwa

two exported files are output:
- 001113_28873.cwa.RData_30_100_400raw.csv
-NA_30_100_400raw.csv

Do you know why the second output file has an NA value in the filename?

For more than two files, many exported files contain the NAs, overwriting them, and preventing to associate each exported file to its corresponding input. 

Thanks,
Joan

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Exported Files with NA identifier
parts:
Hi Joan,

Are the ID and filename correctly recognized in the part2 csv report "part2_summary.csv"?

If not, what value did you use for argument 'idloc'? Probably you need to use idloc = 2 such that it uses the filename as identifier rather attempting to extract the ID from the filename.

Did you work with the data on different machines? If yes, how does it go when you process a raw file like '002492_41265.cwa' from binary all the way to part5 on a single computer?

Less likely, but an other route to investigate: The first part of the new filename (the part that is NA in your filename) is generated from the output of R command sort(dir(x)) where 'x' is the path to the directory where the "meta/ms5.out/....RData" files are stored.
What happens if you apply sort(dir(x)) to that directory path on the R command line (or also known as console window)? Do you see NA values? If yes, then maybe the directory is filled with empty filenames or somehow filenames R cannot recognize.

If this does not address it, can you create a new issue on https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues? There is a better place for discussing specific issues like yours, that do not have a quick answer.

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Exported Files with NA identifier
parts:
Hi Vincent, 

Thanks for your reply. 

I was using idloc=1 and getting incorrect identification in part2_summary.csv. I've changed it to idloc=2 and fixed this but it did not solve the NA identifiers in ms5.outraw. 

I am running all parts in the same computer. 

Investigating how the filenames are built, I've found that filenames in ms5.outraw are derived from filenames in ms5.out, but the latter are not yet there when ms5.outraw files are saved. So, I guess that this might cause the NA identifiers. In fact, I've changed the code to derived filenames from ms3.out and it seems to solve my problem. I've opened an issue in github https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/124

Best,
Joan
